audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a $593 million litigation windfall
audit_findings.magnitude: $441 million after tax, equal to 13.8% of the $3,188.9 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring gain retained in anchor OE would be compounded and capitalized throughout the DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of these lump-sum settlements, we recorded gains within SG&A Expenses of $ 593 million, net of legal fees.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the settlement produced a $593 million pretax and $441 million after-tax gain. The supplied calculation does not establish whether it was removed. This is therefore an unresolved calculation issue, not a demonstrated valuation error, but its size relative to anchor OE is plainly material.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2026 OE line by line and rerun all scenarios after separately removing the $441 million settlement benefit while preserving the independent treatment of the $187 million transformation charge.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal or replacement cost may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $142 million principal payment or $152 million finance-lease amortization, equal to 4.5% or 4.8% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back finance-lease amortization through D&A without deducting principal or replacement capital removes the financed asset-consumption cost from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Property and equipment, including assets acquired under finance leases, is depreciated using the straight-line method over estimated useful lives or lease terms if shorter.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes the relevant amounts but the supplied OE calculation does not show their treatment. An omission is therefore possible rather than demonstrated. A recurring deduction of roughly $142–$152 million is large enough to affect the capitalized value materially.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $152 million amortization, $142 million principal payment, and $104 million noncash leased-asset additions through OE, then rerun using one consistent deduction for principal or replacement capital without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter overlooks the scheduled Ulta partnership termination
audit_findings.mechanism: Termination can change post-anchor sales, margins, occupancy economics, traffic, and therefore prospective OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we reached a mutual agreement with Ulta Beauty to terminate our commercial shop-in-shop operating agreement when it expires in August 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The partnership termination is a filed, scheduled perimeter change, while the valuation records no perimeter adjustment. However, Ulta's recurring contribution is not disclosed, and the $64 million of partnership and other termination-related charges is not an estimate of lost recurring economics. The record cannot establish the value impact or even the net direction after avoided costs.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Ulta-specific sales, gross profit, occupancy income, incremental costs, and traffic effects; remove nonrecurring termination charges separately and rerun post-August 2026 OE.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-on may include operating receivables rather than separable excess cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Operating card-settlement receivables or required operating liquidity added in the equity bridge can double count assets already supporting OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash equivalents also include amounts due from third-party financial institutions for credit and debit card transactions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms that cash equivalents include card-settlement receivables. At January 2026 these were $627 million; at August 2026 the $5,411 million balance included $4,337 million of short-term investments, leaving $1,074 million of cash and other cash-equivalent amounts. The current receivable amount and minimum operating-liquidity requirement are not disclosed, so the improper portion of the bridge cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the August 2026 cash-equivalent composition and a supportable minimum-liquidity requirement, then rerun the bridge with only separable excess cash and investments whose income was purged.

audit_findings.title: Near-term capital spending is materially above the anchor-year level
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,273 million gross guided increase, equal to 39.9% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Required maintenance spending reduces near-term OE; growth spending instead belongs in the reinvestment and growth framework and could otherwise be double counted.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect capital expenditures in 2026 of approximately $5 billion to support our store experience and remodel program, continued investment in supply chain and technology projects, and investment in new stores.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed $5 billion guidance exceeds anchor-year property expenditures of $3.727 billion by $1.273 billion, and six-month FY2026 expenditures had already reached $2.404 billion. That gross difference is reasonably capable of materially changing value. The net direction remains unresolved because the maintenance-versus-growth split and any overlap with RONTA-based reinvestment are not supplied.
audit_findings.action: Classify the $5 billion guidance between maintenance, replacement, and growth capital; map timing into the explicit forecast and rerun OE while eliminating overlap with the RONTA reinvestment charge.

audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor predates material post-year-end tariff changes and available interim results
audit_findings.mechanism: A stale OE anchor can omit recurring post-year-end margin, sales, capex, and working-capital changes, while including interim tariff refunds would introduce another nonrecurring gain.
audit_findings.evidence: We are closely monitoring the evolving consumer and regulatory landscape, including new tariffs announced in February 2026 in response to the U.S. Supreme Court ruling on IEEPA tariffs, and adjusting plans as needed.
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated: the bridge and shares use August information while OE ends January 31. The interim filing reports $994 million of pretax tariff refunds, a $1.65 per-share after-tax benefit, $2.658 billion of six-month net earnings, $1.597 billion of D&A, and $2.404 billion of capex. Those figures show material intervening activity, but the recurring tariff burden, further refunds, pricing effects, and normalized interim OE cannot be isolated from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Build a trailing-twelve-month OE reconciliation through August 1, 2026; remove the disclosed tariff-refund benefit and other nonrecurring items, incorporate interim capex and operating performance, and rerun all scenarios.
